title: Configuration
intro.1: Everything is set with environment variables, read once at start. There are two layers: the Compose variables you set in a .env file, and the containers’ own environment.
compose-variables.title: Compose variables
compose-variables.1: compose.yaml reads these from your shell or a .env file next to it and passes them on. After a change, run bash install.sh again: it reads .env and compose.override.yaml.
compose-variables.2: Installed by hand, run in the checkout DOCKER_GID=$(stat -c %g /var/run/docker.sock) docker compose up -d: without DOCKER_GID the controller loses Docker access. Compose reads compose.override.yaml on its own.
compose-variables.3: Other ADMIN_* or CONTROLLER_* names in .env do nothing on their own: Compose passes only what the file names. Set them in an override file instead.

the-controller.title: The controller
session-containers.title: Session containers
session-containers.1: The display, browser, proxy and agent containers get their environment from the controller’s fixed templates; you do not set it. The browser’s CPU and memory come from the controller’s variables above; the display, proxy and agent limits are fixed. The walled-garden settings are under Public demo.
running-more-than-one.title: Running more than one installation
running-more-than-one.1: Give each installation its own ADMIN_PORT and CONTROLLER_INSTANCE, and its own state, controller and streams volumes (STREAMS_VOLUME names one explicitly, so a different Compose project name alone is not enough).
